article.name: dsh-auto-memory
article.summary: A DeepSeek Harness plugin that stores typed memories as scoped Markdown files, injects a byte-bounded index, and adds trust states, transcript evidence for optional consolidation, lexical search, and injection audit. This is a source review; the system, tests, and benchmark workloads were not run.

who_what.text: Catalog ordinal 197 identifies dsh-auto-memory with the explicit AskTheWay/dsh-auto-memory repository locator. The pinned Atlas roster entry is recorded only for curated identity and locator attribution, not as assessment evidence.

The official repository presents dsh-auto-memory as a DeepSeek Harness plugin that provides local persistent memory. The inspected README does not identify a more specific maintainer or publish a contact email.

The official repository page identifies main as default. The main Atom feed reports current head ac3cfd4ba161adf9b48f01238e58d677a55cb09b updated 2026-11-23T14:24:50Z; the commit page identifies the same revision on main.

architecture.text: Each record is a Markdown file with YAML frontmatter and body; MEMORY.md is regenerated as a derived index. Records support four types, user/project scopes, trust state, evidence, expiry, keywords, read metadata and lifecycle links.

Project directories are derived from the owning session cwd; the user directory is shared across workspaces. Tool guards reject project-scope operations without a trusted session cwd and remove user scope from all paths when disabled.
The plugin wires tools, a prompt section, optional disposal-time consolidation, and a web panel. No separate hosted service or embedding store is required.

behavior.text: memory_write creates or updates a named record. Without explicit scope, it finds an existing same-name record in an available scope and updates that layer, otherwise it writes to project scope. The store sanitizes and atomically writes under a cross-process lock, then rebuilds the derived index.

Automatic consolidation is disabled by default. If enabled, bounded session text is sent to a model at root-agent disposal; validated proposals are stored as candidates. Failures are logged and do not interrupt the session; buffered material can be lost on process crash before writing.

Direct deletion removes a selected memory file. Disable, expiry and stale zero-read eviction suppress injection while retaining the file. Bulk prune and delete-all are guarded by approval; delete-all additionally requires confirmation. File deletion does not establish secure erasure from backups or later re-extraction.

Prompt assembly injects a byte-bounded index wrapped as stored data. The first user message freezes that session's selection; tool reads see writes immediately, while later prompt injection sees them in the next session. With both scopes over budget, project memory receives a guaranteed share.

Explicit search is lexical, coverage-ranked and limited to eight results; excerpts and reads carry trust/lifecycle notes. No vector or embedding retrieval path was found in the inspected search implementation.

evidence.text: Records can carry candidate, verified, disputed or superseded status, plus evidence containing a source session ID and quote. The panel is the user-controlled verification path; content changes downgrade trust and invalidate prior evidence.

Consolidation quotes originate in model proposals and are checked against captured transcript text. They support traceability to a conversation but do not establish independent source citations or factual correctness.
The store applies an injection-pattern guard and the prompt labels injected content as data, not instructions. Candidate records may still be injected; disputed and superseded records are excluded.

observability.text: The append-only JSONL audit records session, cwd, injected and truncated entries, byte count, configured budget and whether selection was frozen. Appends are serialized and the file is rotated at a size limit; failures do not block prompt assembly.

The panel exposes injection/truncation statistics, reads, health findings, and the latest consolidation outcome. Source-visible locking, atomic replacement and bounded prompt bytes are design properties, not measured performance.

limits.text: This review covered the README and selected current sources for records, storage, tools, prompt assembly, retrieval, consolidation and audit. It did not inspect every panel, import/export, host integration, or deployment path, and did not use a local upstream checkout.

Source inspection does not establish deployed isolation, extraction quality, effective security, physical deletion completeness, real-world recall, load behavior, latency, cost or storage efficiency. No system, tests or benchmark workload was run.
